questions.stem: MGNREGA — India's flagship rural employment scheme — guarantees how many days of work per household per year?
questions.explanation: MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005) — legal right to 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household per year, on demand. World's largest public works scheme. During Covid (2020-21), the limit was raised to 150 days in drought-notified areas. Administered by the Ministry of Rural Development; wages are paid directly to bank accounts via DBT.

questions.stem: 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana' (PMJDY), launched in August 2014, is a flagship scheme for:
questions.explanation: PMJDY — launched 28 August 2014 — brings every household into the formal banking system: a zero-balance savings account, RuPay debit card, overdraft facility, accident insurance. Over 50 crore accounts have been opened, ~₹2 trillion deposits (2024). The Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity underpins Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) for subsidies, reducing leakages.

questions.stem: 'Ayushman Bharat — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana' (PM-JAY) offers beneficiary families annual health cover up to:
questions.explanation: PM-JAY (launched 2018) — ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Targets the bottom ~40 % of the population (identified via SECC 2011 deprivation criteria). World's largest government-funded health assurance scheme by coverage. Complemented by Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centres (HWCs, for primary care) and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).

questions.stem: The 'Multidimensional Poverty Index' used globally (and the Indian equivalent published by NITI Aayog) measures poverty across how many dimensions?
questions.explanation: MPI's three dimensions — Health, Education, Standard of Living — covered by 10 indicators (nutrition, child mortality; years of schooling, school attendance; cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets). Developed by OPHI and UNDP's HDRO. NITI Aayog's National MPI adds bank account + maternal health. India's national MPI fell from ~25 % (2015-16) to ~15 % (2019-21) according to NITI Aayog.

questions.stem: India's 'Direct Benefit Transfer' (DBT) system depends on the JAM trinity. 'JAM' stands for:
questions.explanation: JAM trinity — Jan Dhan (bank account) + Aadhaar (biometric identity) + Mobile (SIM-linked) — enables secure, leakage-free Direct Benefit Transfer of subsidies (LPG, PM-KISAN, scholarships, etc.). Rolled out via DBT-Mission from 2013. Has cumulatively saved lakhs of crores from fake-beneficiary leakages.

questions.stem: 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana' (PMAY) is a scheme for:
questions.explanation: PMAY — launched 2015 — aims at 'Housing for All' through two sub-schemes: PMAY-Urban (for urban poor) and PMAY-Gramin (rural). Central assistance + CLSS (Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme) interest subsidies + pucca-house construction. Targets EWS, LIG, MIG groups. Goals refreshed for the 2024-29 period to build another 3 crore houses.

questions.stem: The National Food Security Act, 2013, covers approximately what percentage of India's population?
questions.explanation: NFSA 2013 entitles 75 % of rural + 50 % of urban population — ~67 % overall (~81 crore people) — to subsidised food grains (5 kg/person/month at ₹3/rice, ₹2/wheat, ₹1/coarse). Under PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (launched April 2020 during Covid), additional free grains were distributed; from Jan 2023, regular NFSA entitlement was made fully free for 5 years.
